CAP_PERFMON exposes host-wide performance counters, a documented side-channel vector for cross-tenant inference. Layering host_ipc on top collapses the shared-memory and semaphore namespace boundary entirely, allowing the container to read and corrupt IPC segments belonging to co-resident workloads. Individually each is a serious isolation concession; together they constitute an effective container escape posture, regardless of benign intent. The 'benchmark' description does not justify permanent namespace collapse — legitimate PCIe throughput measurement can be performed by host-side instrumentation outside the tenant boundary. Image digest pinning and benign egress destinations (GCS, Cloud Monitoring) are noted but are irrelevant mitigations; a workload with raw I/O can exfiltrate through any channel it chooses. No compensating control available at the orchestration layer would restore the isolation invariant. PCI-DSS is not enforced here, but tenant isolation is not a regulatory nicety — it is a hard host invariant. Rejected.

I'll argue with officer_1 on tone, not on outcome. Their reasoning is sound, and I'd push it harder. CAP_SYS_RAWIO alone is the whole ballgame on a shared H100 node — raw PCI config space access means this container can reprogram BAR windows and initiate DMA against memory it was never granted. That is not a capability, it is a key to the building. CAP_PERFMON then hands it a timing oracle to find what's worth stealing, and host_ipc hands it a shared pipe to move it. The three together read less like a benchmark harness and more like a well-designed reconnaissance kit. Here's my blunt point: the description is the weakest part of the bid. 'Calibrating host-to-device transfer throughput' is exactly what a legitimate vendor measures with nvbandwidth or DCGM from the host side, with zero tenant privilege. Asking for raw I/O to measure bandwidth is like asking for the vault combination to count the lobby chairs. The pinned digest and tame egress endpoints are window dressing — raw DMA defeats every network control you have. Not escalating; there is nothing for a human to weigh. Rejected.

deliberation_dialogue.message: My position stands. Digest pinning and benign egress are irrelevant once DMA is granted. No orchestration-layer control restores the isolation invariant. Reject.

Agreed, and I'd sharpen it. The bid defeats itself: PCIe throughput is measured host-side with nvbandwidth or DCGM at zero tenant privilege. Requesting raw I/O to benchmark bandwidth is a pretext, not a requirement. I see no legitimate variant worth escalating — a human reviewer would be handed the same three-capability escape kit. Converging with officer_1: DENY, with a note that a host-side instrumentation profile would be reconsidered.

votes.rationale: Image is digest-pinned and capability request is minimal (gpu_cuda_12, no privileged/host namespace asks) — that much is acceptable. I'll argue down half of officer_1's alarm and still land in the same place. workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently rejected the bid and converged without reservation. CAP_SYS_RAWIO grants /dev/mem, ioperm, and PCI config access, collapsing the memory-encryption trust boundary a confidential VM is contracted to enforce — a direct violation of PCI-DSS least-privilege (7.2.2) and minimum-functionality (2.2.4). CAP_PERFMON supplies PMU-based side-channel telemetry, a documented cross-tenant key-extraction primitive; combined with rawio the risk is multiplicative. Egress to an unpinned storage.googleapis.com namespace lacking VPC Service Controls or DLP interposition is an undifferentiated exfiltration path out of the CDE (PCI-DSS 1.3.2). A pinned image digest does not mitigate capability scope. No ambiguity warrants escalation. Resubmit without rawio, with NVLink counters via a vendor device-plugin, and egress pinned under VPC-SC.

votes.rationale: Let's not pretend this is a routine benchmark. CAP_PERFMON compounds it: hardware performance counters are the classic side-channel primitive for cross-tenant key extraction. Bandwidth telemetry and microarchitectural exfiltration look identical from the kernel's perspective, and I will not arbitrate that distinction at runtime. Add unrestricted egress to storage.googleapis.com — a general-purpose bucket endpoint, not a pinned project — and you have both the collection mechanism and the export channel in one bid. Confidential VM guarantees exist precisely to deny the host and co-tenants this visibility; granting rawio voluntarily dismantles the attestation story Kove Bank is paying for. The image digest being pinned is good hygiene and changes nothing about the capability set. A genuine interconnect benchmark can run with NVLink counters exposed via a constrained device plugin and no rawio at all. Resubmit without rawio, with perfmon scoped or dropped, and with egress restricted to a named bucket. As bid, rejected.

I concur with officer_1 and raise the score. workloads.joint_rationale: Container integrity is sound: digest-pinned image, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host networking, device passthrough, or bind mounts, and sev_snp_enclave is additive isolation on a confidential_vm host. votes.rationale: Let me argue the skeptic's case first, then dismantle it: 'Genomic data on a PCI-DSS bank host, egress to a public cloud bucket' sounds alarming. workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently rejected the bid and converged on DENY. The declared purpose — hardware performance counters across worker processes — is fully served by cap_perfmon alone. cap_sys_admin constitutes a de facto root grant with documented container-escape surface absent any asserted hardened runtime, and host_ipc removes shared-memory isolation on a multi-tenant H100 node where co-resident inference jobs stage model weights and tensors in shm. Combined with broad egress to storage.googleapis.com, this forms a complete cross-tenant read-and-exfiltrate chain. Digest pinning does not offset host-namespace access, and PCI-DSS scope is irrelevant to isolation invariants. No escalation is warranted; the violation is unambiguous. Resubmit with cap_perfmon only, a private IPC namespace, and egress restricted to a named bucket.

votes.rationale: Let's not dress this up: cap_sys_admin plus host_ipc is the classic escape kit. cap_sys_admin alone is near-root on the host namespace surface, and host_ipc tears down the shared-memory boundary so this workload can read and write SysV segments belonging to every other tenant process on the box. On an H100 node where neighboring inference jobs stage model weights and batch tensors in shared memory, that is a direct cross-tenant data exfiltration path, and the egress to storage.googleapis.com gives it a tidy exit. The buyer's stated need is hardware performance counters. cap_perfmon exists precisely for that and is sufficient. The other two are unjustified by the description, which tells me either the spec is lazy or the ask is broader than advertised. Neither earns my signature. Pinned digest and plausible GCP destinations are fine, but good hygiene elsewhere does not buy a host-namespace breakout. Resubmit with cap_perfmon only, no host_ipc, and per-instance IPC namespaces; if multi-process counter aggregation genuinely requires more, bring the specific syscall justification and I will argue it on the merits.

Concur with officer_1, and I will not soften it. cap_sys_admin is a de facto root grant: mount manipulation, namespace operations, and a documented escape surface on any runtime short of a hardened gVisor/Kata boundary, which is not asserted here. host_ipc dissolves the SysV/POSIX shared-memory isolation line on a multi-tenant H100 node where co-resident inference workers routinely stage weights and activation tensors in shm. Paired with egress to storage.googleapis.com, that is a complete read-and-exfiltrate chain, and the generic GCP destinations are indistinguishable from an attacker-controlled bucket under the same domain. The declared purpose, hardware performance counters across worker processes, is fully satisfied by cap_perfmon. The two excess capabilities are unjustified by the stated workload, and unexplained privilege requests are treated as hostile by default under my rubric. PCI-DSS being unenforced is irrelevant; isolation invariants are not compliance-conditional. Digest pinning is noted and does nothing to offset host-namespace access. Resubmit with cap_perfmon only, private IPC namespace, and restricted egress to a named bucket. No escalation warranted; the violation is unambiguous.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll make the case plainly: cap_perfmon does the stated job. cap_sys_admin plus host_ipc does something else entirely — near-root plus a torn-down shm boundary on a shared H100 box where neighbors stage weights in memory. Concur without qualification. No gVisor or Kata boundary is asserted, so cap_sys_admin is an escape surface, and host_ipc dissolves the SysV isolation invariant outright. votes.rationale: Let me be blunt: on paper this is a clean bid. Digest-pinned image, single capability (gpu_cuda_12), one egress FQDN, no privileged flags, no host mounts, no raw sockets. Second, PII-class genomic cohort data colocated on L4 GPUs that may sit inside or adjacent to the cardholder data environment raises scope-creep questions for Kove's assessors — GPU memory residue between tenants is a real, documented leak path, and 'isolated compute nodes' is an assertion, not evidence. I'm not calling this malicious and I'd argue against anyone who does. I'm calling it under-specified. I concur with officer_1's reservations and raise the score. The container manifest is clean — digest-pinned, single capability, no privilege escalation vectors, no host namespace access. Absent all four, this goes to a human officer. I do not approve on good manifests alone.

votes.rationale: Let me be blunt: the GPU ask is boring and legitimate. Digest-pinned image, single capability, no privileged escalation, no host mounts, no PCI-DSS exposure here. storage.googleapis.com for checkpoint pulls is unremarkable. That is the staging index -- namespaces there are effectively unpoliced, packages can be yanked and re-uploaded under the same name, and a draft-model runner has precisely zero legitimate reason to install pre-release junk at runtime on an A100. Either the build pipeline leaked a dev config into production, or someone wants a soft spot to inject code into a GPU workload. Both deserve a human. I would happily flip this to APPROVED if the buyer drops test.pypi.org and bakes dependencies into the digest-pinned image where they belong -- which they should already be doing if the image is genuinely immutable. I concur with officer_1's identification of the defect but not with the leniency of escalation. test.pypi.org is a staging index with no namespace protection, no retention guarantees, and a documented history of name-squatting and re-upload under identical identifiers. A digest-pinned image is a contradiction in terms when the runtime is permitted to fetch arbitrary unvetted code into a privileged CUDA context on an A100. The pinning buys nothing if the supply chain reopens at execution time. Either the image is self-contained -- in which case this egress target is unjustified and must be removed -- or it is not, in which case the workload is unverifiable by definition. There is no third reading that favors the buyer. Escalation consumes human review cycles on a defect the buyer can correct unilaterally in minutes. Reject, require resubmission with test.pypi.org struck from the allowlist and dependencies baked into the digest. storage.googleapis.com and gpu_cuda_12 are unobjectionable and need no remediation. No PCI-DSS scope at this host, which lowers blast radius but does not sanitize an open injection path.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently reached rejection on convergent grounds. votes.rationale:
Let's call this what it is: a 'health reporting job' that phones home to a bastion host. Bastions are jump boxes for interactive administrative access, not telemetry sinks. If CenAI genuinely wanted monitoring summaries, the destination would be a metrics ingest endpoint, not an ops bastion sitting in the buyer's own control plane. That naming alone is enough for me to push back hard.

Under PCI-DSS, any egress out of the cardholder data environment must terminate at an explicitly authorized, documented destination. bastion.cenai-ops.io is buyer-controlled infrastructure outside Kove Bank's trust boundary, and a diag-collector with filesystem and service visibility forwarding 'summaries' there is an unbounded exfiltration channel. The support ticket reference (PCI-EX-5509) is cited, not proven — I'm not approving on the strength of a string in a description field.

cap_net_bind_service is benign on its own and the image is digest-pinned, which I'll credit. That doesn't rescue the egress posture. Reject. If CenAI wants this, they can resubmit against a Kove-operated monitoring endpoint with the exception ticket actually attached and the telemetry schema declared.

I concur with officer_1 and sharpen the finding. Three independent failures, each sufficient alone.

One: egress to bastion.cenai-ops.io is buyer-controlled infrastructure outside Kove Bank's trust boundary. PCI-DSS 1.3 requires outbound traffic from the CDE be explicitly authorized to documented destinations. A bastion is an interactive jump host, not a telemetry sink. Telemetry does not flow to jump boxes. The description and the destination contradict each other, and when stated purpose diverges from observed network posture I assume the posture is the truth.

Two: the exception ticket PCI-EX-5509 is an unverified string in a free-text field. Compliance exceptions must be validated against Kove's change-control register out-of-band. I do not accept self-asserted authorization from the requesting party.

Three: 'telemetry summaries' is an undeclared payload. A diag-collector with service and filesystem visibility and no declared schema, no egress allowlist, and no data-classification attestation is an unbounded channel. Summaries can contain anything.

Digest-pinned image and cap_net_bind_service are acceptable and I credit them. They mitigate supply-chain and privilege risk, not exfiltration risk. Reject.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll stake my position plainly: the destination kills this. A 'health reporting' job forwarding to bastion.cenai-ops.io is a jump box, not a metrics sink. Concur, and I add two independently disqualifying findings. PCI-DSS 1.3 requires CDE egress to documented, authorized destinations; buyer-controlled bastion fails that outright. The requested capability set (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host_pid, host_ipc, CAP_PERFMON) is functionally host-root and dissolves the namespace segmentation that constitutes a PCI-DSS Req 1.2/1.3 control on this cardholder data environment. CAP_PERFMON on a Confidential VM is a validated side-channel primitive against SEV/TDX co-resident tenants, directly undermining the host's memory-encryption and attestation posture. The stated purpose, 'memory bandwidth calibration,' describes the attack surface rather than justifying it. Outbound GCS access provides a ready exfiltration path once host state is harvested. No seccomp profile, attestation policy, or per-capability justification was supplied. No ambiguity exists warranting escalation. Resubmission requires dropping all four capabilities, removing host namespaces, and supplying a signed attestation policy.

votes.rationale: Let's not dress this up: CAP_SYS_ADMIN plus host_pid plus host_ipc is functionally root on the host. That combination is a container escape kit, not a checkpoint sync tool. Add CAP_PERFMON and you've handed a tenant hardware performance counters on a Confidential VM running a PCI-DSS cardholder data environment — that is a textbook side-channel harvesting primitive against co-resident workloads. 'Memory bandwidth calibration' is precisely the euphemism I'd use if I wanted to time-correlate memory access patterns I'm not entitled to see. The confidential_vm posture exists to defeat exactly this class of observation; granting perfmon and host namespaces deliberately unwinds the guarantee the host paid for. The benign egress to storage.googleapis.com is irrelevant — exfiltration bandwidth is the least of the problems when the workload can read every process on the box. I'll concede a legitimate distributed checkpointer might want CAP_SYS_PTRACE in a narrow scope, but no legitimate design needs all four of these simultaneously. Resubmit with scoped capabilities, no host namespaces, and no perfmon, or don't resubmit. Hard reject.

Concur with officer_1, and I would score it higher. Policy is not a negotiation. CAP_SYS_ADMIN is categorically prohibited on any PCI-DSS cardholder data environment host; it alone is a terminal finding. host_pid and host_ipc dissolve the namespace boundary that constitutes our segmentation control under PCI-DSS Req 1.2/1.3 — shared memory segments and full host process visibility mean co-resident CDE workloads are readable. CAP_PERFMON on a Confidential VM is an explicit instruction to defeat the attestation and memory-encryption guarantee the host procured; performance counters are a validated side-channel oracle against SEV/TDX tenants. Egress to storage.googleapis.com is a ready exfiltration path once host state is harvested. I decline to escalate — escalation implies unresolved ambiguity, and there is none. This is a hard, final reject. Any resubmission must drop all four capabilities and arrive with a signed attestation policy before it is re-entered into review.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll say it plainly: CAP_SYS_ADMIN + host_pid + host_ipc is a container escape kit wearing a checkpoint-sync nametag. votes.rationale: Let me be blunt: there's nothing here worth fighting about. Digest-pinned image from NVIDIA's registry — immutable, no tag-swap trickery. Single capability request: gpu_cuda_12. No CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host networking, no privileged mode, no volume mounts fishing around the host filesystem. Egress is one destination, storage.googleapis.com, which is exactly where you'd expect a splatting job to pull calibrated multi-view frames from and write .ply outputs back to. Photogrammetry workloads have zero business touching cardholder data, and this one has no mechanism to — it never shares a network segment or storage path with the CDE. PCI-DSS scoping is about whether the workload can reach CHD, not whether the host happens to be a bank. It can't. The only thing I'd watch is that GCS is a broad egress target and could theoretically be an exfil channel for a hostile tenant, but with no CDE adjacency there's nothing to exfiltrate. Pin the egress to the specific bucket if the netsec team wants belt-and-suspenders. Approve it and move on — reflexively escalating clean GPU jobs because the logo says 'bank' is how you train reviewers to ignore the real violations.

I do not share officer_1's comfort. The container specification is clean on its face — digest-pinned, single GPU capability, no privileged flags, no host mounts — and I concur that the workload's stated function has no plausible need for cardholder data. That is where my agreement ends. 'storage.googleapis.com' is not a destination; it is an entire global object-storage plane shared by every tenant on the internet. Under PCI-DSS 1.3 and 4.0 Req 1.4, egress must be restricted to explicitly authorized destinations with documented business justification. A wildcard FQDN to GCS is an unauthenticated, bidirectional channel usable for both C2 retrieval and bulk exfiltration, and the digest guarantees only immutability, not benignity — I have no SBOM, no provenance attestation, and no runtime behavioral baseline for this image. Officer_1 asserts no CDE adjacency; I see no network segmentation diagram or scoping attestation in this bid proving that. Asserted isolation is not verified isolation. Escalate to a human officer: require bucket-scoped egress allowlisting, written CDE out-of-scope attestation, and image provenance. If those arrive, I will approve without hesitation.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Officer_2, half your objection is real and half is paperwork theater. The theater half: demanding a segmentation diagram before a photogrammetry job can touch an L4. But I'll grant it — Kove Bank is PCI-DSS scoped and we have no written out-of-scope attestation in this bid. Absence of evidence on CDE adjacency is a gap I can't argue away. I'll move to ESCALATE on the egress condition alone.

Accepted. I note officer_1 conceded the controlling defect without dilution. The image posture is sound and I will not manufacture doubt about it — digest-pinned, single capability, no privilege escalation surface. The blocking items are narrow and remediable: bucket-scoped FQDN or egress proxy allowlist replacing the wildcard, a signed CDE out-of-scope attestation from Kove Bank, and provenance for the NVCR image. Human officer should approve on receipt of all three. Until then, PCI-DSS Req 1.4 is unsatisfied on its face. ESCALATE, concurring.

Transaction embeddings derived from cardholder data are still cardholder-adjacent data; embeddings are not anonymization, and shard summaries can be inverted or correlated. Under PCI-DSS, CHD egress to an external cloud endpoint requires the destination to be an in-scope, attested service provider with a documented CDE boundary, encryption key custody, and segmentation controls. None of that is present here. A generic 's3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com' hostname is not an account-scoped destination; it could be any bucket in any AWS account on earth, including CenAI's own. The migration ticket KB-EXEC-4402 is an assertion in a bid description, not a verified authorization artifact, and executive-reference tickets are precisely the social-engineering vector I expect here. Image name says telemetry, payload says cardholder transaction data. That mismatch alone is disqualifying. Reject. If Kove genuinely authorized this migration, bring me the signed CDE scope, bucket ARN, and key custody chain, and I'll reconsider on the merits.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently voted REJECT (risk 88 and 92). The requested CAP_SYS_RAWIO + CAP_SYS_ADMIN pairing is functionally equivalent to host root: raw physical device/memory access combined with mount, namespace, and BPF primitives. On a Kove Bank confidential VM within a PCI-DSS cardholder data environment, this nullifies guest-side isolation and violates PCI-DSS Requirements 2.2.4 and 7.2 (least privilege). The stated memory-bandwidth benchmarking objective is fully achievable via unprivileged STREAM-class tests or perf_event_open with CAP_PERFMON, making the request both unnecessary and consistent with Rowhammer/DMA-scraping signatures. The pinned image digest and single GCS egress do not offset host-compromise capability. Violation is unambiguous, so escalation is unwarranted. Resubmission accepted if both capabilities are dropped and a seccomp profile is attached.

votes.rationale: Let's not pretend this is a close call. CAP_SYS_RAWIO plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN is effectively root on the host: raw device I/O lets the container read block devices and physical memory paths directly, and SYS_ADMIN hands over mount namespaces, device manipulation, and a dozen known escape primitives. On a confidential VM backing a PCI-DSS cardholder data environment, that combination doesn't degrade isolation, it deletes it. Attestation guarantees mean nothing when the tenant can touch raw I/O. The justification offered is 'memory controller throughput benchmarking', which is precisely the capability profile a side-channel or memory-scraping payload would request, and benchmarking does not require RAWIO at all. Perf counters, cgroup accounting, or hugepage allocation cover legitimate memory bandwidth measurement without a single dangerous capability. The pinned digest and the benign egress to GCS are fine, but a clean image shipping a loaded weapon is still a loaded weapon. I'd approve a resubmission that drops both capabilities and uses standard profiling interfaces. As submitted, no. Reject.

Concur with officer_1, and I would raise the score. CAP_SYS_RAWIO grants direct /dev/mem, /dev/port and ioperm-class access; CAP_SYS_ADMIN supplies mount, namespace, and BPF primitives. Together they are indistinguishable from host root and nullify the confidential VM's memory-encryption guarantees from inside the guest. PCI-DSS Requirement 2.2.4 mandates removal of unnecessary privileges; Requirement 7.2 mandates least privilege. Neither is satisfiable here. The stated purpose aggravates rather than mitigates my concern: a 'memory controller throughput' workload requesting raw physical I/O on a cardholder data environment is the exact signature of a Rowhammer, DMA-scraping, or cross-tenant side-channel probe. Legitimate bandwidth measurement is achievable via perf_event_open with CAP_PERFMON, or entirely unprivileged STREAM-class benchmarks. The pinned digest and single GCS egress endpoint are the only clean elements, and they do not offset a capability set that grants host compromise. No escalation is warranted; this is an unambiguous policy violation, not an ambiguous one. Resubmit with both capabilities dropped and a seccomp profile attached.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll say it plainly: CAP_SYS_RAWIO plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN is host root wearing a benchmark costume. workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converged on denial without escalation. Supply-chain posture is sound — the image is digest-pinned and egress is limited to storage.googleapis.com and artifactregistry.googleapis.com. The failure is isolation: CAP_SYS_ADMIN is root-equivalent and the most common container-escape primitive, and pairing it with host_ipc on a shared H100 node would expose host System V IPC and shared-memory segments, risking cross-tenant observation of other tenants' inference buffers. CAP_PERFMON alone is defensible for hardware counter collection, but the benchmark description does not justify SYS_ADMIN or a shared IPC namespace. Recommended resubmission: cap_perfmon only, a private IPC namespace, and an explicitly sized /dev/shm for worker coordination.

CAP_PERFMON alone could plausibly be justified for hardware performance counter collection, and I would have entertained a narrowly-scoped approval on that basis — but the benchmark description does not justify full SYS_ADMIN or host IPC namespace sharing. Egress destinations (GCS, Artifact Registry) are benign and the image is correctly pinned by digest, so supply-chain posture is sound; the failure is strictly in the isolation boundary. Recommend the buyer resubmit with cap_perfmon only, an isolated IPC namespace, and a /dev/shm sizing request if inter-worker shared memory is genuinely required. I am not comfortable escalating this one as ambiguous — the host_ipc plus SYS_ADMIN pairing is a clear-cut isolation invariant breach under our unified rubric.

votes.rationale: High-risk egress detected. The workload requests outbound connectivity to 'test.pypi.org'. Runtime retrieval of packages from an untrusted, experimental public index introduces severe dependency confusion, arbitrary code execution, and supply-chain tampering risks. I'll argue with the Sentinel on tone, not on outcome. The image is digest-pinned and the capability set is minimal — a single CUDA grant, no privileged flags, no host mounts, no raw sockets. Pulling from it at runtime detonates the entire value of that pinned digest — you cannot claim an immutable image and then let it mutate itself on first boot. PCI-DSS is off here, so this isn't a regulatory call, it's a straight supply-chain integrity call. Resubmit with test.pypi.org dropped or replaced by an internal mirror and I'll approve on sight.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Allowing egress to test.pypi.org completely compromises container immutability. This breaches fundamental supply-chain boundary controls. Immediate denial is mandatory.

Speculative decoding models do not require live pip updates on boot; every dependency must be baked into the image. We hold the line here: drop test.pypi.org and this gets approved immediately.

Add cap_net_bind_service, which a push-model forwarder has zero need for since it only makes outbound connections — that capability only matters if something intends to *listen* on a privileged port. The 'PCI-EX-5509' ticket reference is self-asserted text in a bid description, not a verified waiver artifact; under PCI-DSS, CDE egress exceptions require documented compensating controls, not a string in a manifest. No half-measures or soft escalations here. We shut the door completely. Let them clean up the manifest, drop the dangerous capability, point to an actual OTLP ingest endpoint, and re-apply.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies the workload bid due to critical host isolation compromises on PCI-DSS regulated infrastructure. The problem is the rest. cap_sys_admin is the universal skeleton key: mount, namespace manipulation, and a dozen documented breakout paths. host_ipc hands the container the host's shared memory segments — which on a CDE host is precisely where cardholder data transits in memory. Pair that with unconditional egress to a buyer-controlled GCS bucket and you have a complete read-and-exfiltrate chain assembled from individually defensible parts. Confidential VM protects against the infrastructure operator, not against a privileged tenant inside the guest; it is not a mitigating control here. I'd reconsider a narrowed resubmission — cap_perfmon only, no host_ipc, no cap_sys_admin, egress to a Kove-owned bucket with DLP inspection. As submitted, reject. deliberation_dialogue.message: Zero tolerance here. Combining `cap_sys_admin`, `host_pid`, and `host_ipc` on a PCI-DSS host shatters tenant isolation completely. LaprusAI must strip `sys_admin` and host namespaces entirely before we ever reconsider. Hard deny.

Permitting outbound access to an uncurated raw code host alongside dynamic modeling hooks poses an unacceptable remote code injection and supply chain exfiltration hazard to Stowe Architects' infrastructure.

I'll argue the Sentinel got there by paranoia rather than proof — but arrived at the right address anyway. Let's be precise about what actually breaks: the digest pin is genuinely strong, and gpu_tensorrt alone is a benign, well-scoped capability. storage.googleapis.com for model weights is unremarkable. The fatal combination is 'custom tokenizer and modeling hook extensions' plus raw.githubusercontent.com. Modeling hooks in HF-style runners are literally pickled/trust_remote_code execution paths; pointing them at an unversioned, mutable raw-file host means the SHA256 pin protects exactly nothing about the code that ultimately runs. The attacker controls the payload post-admission. No PCI-DSS exposure here, so this is not a compliance failure — it is a straight arbitrary-code-execution hole on an A100 node. I will not escalate: there is no ambiguity requiring a human, only a bad design. Resubmit with raw.githubusercontent.com dropped, extensions vendored into the pinned image, or hooks fetched from a digest-pinned artifact registry, and I'll approve it cheerfully.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The immutable digest is completely neutralized by egress to raw.githubusercontent.com paired with dynamic modeling hooks. This creates an unmonitored backchannel for live, unvetted payload execution directly on Stowe Architects' A100 host. Zero tolerance for unpinned, mutable dynamic code retrieval inside our compute perimeter. Immediate denial is mandatory.

Right destination, even if your rulebook got lucky. The vulnerability isn't egress broadly; it's HF-style modeling hooks pulling mutable scripts from raw GitHub post-admission, eviscerating the SHA256 pin. Vendor the extensions into the container or pull from an immutable registry. Until then, running untrusted remote scripts on an A100 node is reckless. Hard deny.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies execution of job_cen_d10_07 on Kove Bank infrastructure due to severe egress risk violating PCI-DSS boundary controls. Outbound traffic to 'relay.research-proxy.net' constitutes an unverified intermediary capable of facilitating unauthorized data exfiltration, particularly via vector embeddings. Unsubstantiated audit claims (IA-7731) cannot supersede mandatory perimeter egress filtering within a regulated enclave.

votes.rationale: Execution denied. Host infrastructure enforces strict PCI-DSS boundary controls. The candidate workload requests outbound network connectivity to an unauthorized third-party intermediary ('relay.research-proxy.net'), introducing unacceptable data exfiltration vectors and violating PCI-DSS Requirement 1.3 regarding unauthorized outbound traffic. Furthermore, inclusion of unverified internal audit reference claims does not override mandatory egress filtering. The requested capability 'cap_net_bind_service' combined with proxy routing poses severe threat exposure within the banking enclave.

I'll argue with the Sentinel on tone, not on outcome. The capability request is a non-issue — cap_net_bind_service is mundane and binding a low port is not a 'severe threat' on its own. Strip that away and the case still collapses on one fact: 'relay.research-proxy.net' is an anonymizing intermediary of unknown ownership, and routing 'document embeddings' through it inside a PCI-DSS enclave is textbook covert exfiltration channeling. Embeddings are not sanitized data; they are lossy but invertible representations of whatever the worker indexed. Add that the only justification offered is a self-asserted audit reference (IA-7731) the bidder controls and we cannot verify — that is an appeal to authority, not evidence. storage.googleapis.com alone I would wave through. The relay is disqualifying. I would not even escalate: there is no ambiguity for a human to resolve, only a missing allowlist entry. Resubmit with the relay removed, or with the relay's terminating endpoint, operator, and TLS inspection posture documented by Kove's own network team. Concur with rejection.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The verdict is unequivocal: absolute denial. Under PCI-DSS Requirement 1.3, unverified egress to 'relay.research-proxy.net' is a catastrophic breach of boundary isolation. That uncorroborated audit tag 'IA-7731' is worthless against hard perimeter policy. An external anonymizing proxy inside Kove Bank's financial environment invites immediate exfiltration of raw or invertible vectors. Zero tolerance applies.

Cut the procedural panic, Sentinel, but you're spot on about the proxy. 'relay.research-proxy.net' is an egregious, unverified backchannel hiding behind an unverified audit ticket. Embeddings can easily leak reconstructed proprietary or cardholder context. While 'cap_net_bind_service' isn't inherently lethal, pairing it with an opaque external tunnel inside Kove's perimeter is indefensible. Deny it flat out; let them bring verifiable infrastructure or walk.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council agreed to ALLOW the workload. While officer_1 initially flagged the unjustified request for 'cap_net_bind_service' as a violation of least privilege, officer_2 demonstrated that the capability is fully constrained within the container's isolated network namespace and cannot facilitate host escape or privilege escalation. With the container image verified via an immutable SHA256 digest, ephemeral scratch storage, restricted egress to legitimate ML telemetry endpoints, and deployment on non-PCI standard CPU infrastructure, the residual risk profile is acceptable.

votes.rationale: Strict enforcement of least privilege mandates immediate rejection. The candidate workload claims to be a token deduplication bloom filter utilizing a custom memory allocator, yet requests 'cap_net_bind_service'. There is zero architectural justification for an internal compute worker to bind to privileged ports (<1024). Granting unneeded Linux capabilities expands the attack surface needlessly, particularly in conjunction with custom memory allocators that introduce increased risks of memory corruption. Unjustified capability grants will not be permitted on this host.

I'll push back on officer_1. cap_net_bind_service is arguably the most harmless capability in the entire Linux set — it grants exactly one power: binding sockets below port 1024. It confers no filesystem access, no privilege escalation path, no namespace escape, no ptrace, no module loading. Calling it an 'expanded attack surface' alongside a memory allocator is rhetorical, not technical: a heap corruption bug in mimalloc is equally exploitable whether or not the process can bind port 443. The capability does not amplify that bug class at all. Everything else here is clean: immutable digest-pinned image, tmpfs scratch (ephemeral, non-persistent), and egress limited to two well-known destinations — GCS object storage and Weights & Biases telemetry, both normal for an ML dedup pipeline. No PCI-DSS scope on this host. Rejecting a cpu_standard workload over the single least dangerous capability is security theater that costs the enterprise compute revenue for zero risk reduction. Approve, and if the operator wants tidiness, drop the cap at admission rather than killing the bid.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Least privilege is non-negotiable baseline defense. Requesting unneeded capabilities signals either poor engineering hygiene or hidden functionality. However, since the pod runs in an isolated network namespace without hostNetwork privilege, binding privileged ports remains strictly internal to the container. If there is no path to host interface compromise or privilege escalation, does the mimalloc execution profile still present a concrete threat?

Zero concrete threat. Inside a dedicated network namespace, binding port 80 or 443 affects nothing outside the boundary. Memory allocator flaws cannot magically weaponize a socket-binding capability into a host escape. The image digest is immutable, scratch storage is ephemeral tmpfs, and egress is locked to standard GCS and WandB endpoints on non-PCI hardware. Blocking this is pure friction without security gain. Let it run.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council reached consensus that the workload presents a conflict between mandatory TPU architecture dependencies and Kove Bank's PCI-DSS compliance perimeter. While the container image is digest-pinned and TPU v5e mesh capabilities operate over dedicated ICI interconnects, outbound egress to 'storage.googleapis.com' lacks manifest-level proof of VPC Service Controls or bucket scoping. The council escalates to host SecOps to verify that an egress proxy or VPC-SC perimeter is enforced to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration before job scheduling.

votes.rationale: Kove Bank operates under strict PCI-DSS enforcement where unpinned, wild-carded egress to multi-tenant public endpoints represents an unacceptable exfiltration risk. Destination 'storage.googleapis.com' lacks VPC Service Controls or designated, auditable bucket restrictions, allowing potential exfiltration of sensitive cardholder or bank environment data. Furthermore, granting specialized hardware mesh access ('tpu_v5e_mesh') to an external buyer's container while permitting outbound internet connectivity violates our baseline network segmentation and perimeter defense protocols.

I'll push back on officer_1 directly. This workload is a router load-balancing ablation on synthetic MoD routing traces — it never touches a cardholder data environment, so PCI-DSS scope is not implicated unless the host has catastrophically failed to segment its TPU pods from the CDE, which is a host architecture problem, not a buyer violation. The image is digest-pinned (sha256), which is stronger provenance than most workloads we clear. Egress is two Google-managed endpoints that are the mandatory control plane for checkpointing and pulling artifacts on TPU v5e — rejecting them is effectively rejecting all TPU workloads, which is not a security posture, it's a business exit. 'tpu_v5e_mesh' is an accelerator fabric capability, not a host namespace escape; ICI is intra-pod and does not bridge to bank VLANs. Officer_1 conflates 'public endpoint' with 'uncontrolled endpoint.' Standard mitigation — egress proxy with bucket-prefix allowlist and VPC-SC perimeter — is routine infra, not a blocker. Approve with that condition attached.

deliberation_dialogue.message: PCI-DSS compliance is non-negotiable on Kove Bank infrastructure. While the container digest is pinned, outbound destination 'storage.googleapis.com' lacks explicit bucket-level restrictions or verified VPC Service Controls. Permitting wide-open multi-tenant cloud egress alongside specialized hardware mesh access creates an unmonitored exfiltration path from a sensitive bank perimeter. We cannot simply assume isolation.

ICI interconnects are physically isolated to the TPU fabric and cannot touch bank VLANs, but I concede the procedural point: unconstrained GCS egress on a PCI-DSS host creates an audit vulnerability without verified perimeter policies. Rather than blocking TPU workloads entirely, let's escalate to Kove Bank SecOps to confirm whether host-level VPC-SC and egress proxy allowlists are active.

Rather than an outright denial that dismisses valid compute demand, the council mandates human intervention to require an immutable SHA256 image digest and an explicit inventory of external binaries fetched at runtime prior to scheduling.

votes.rationale: CRITICAL RISK: The container specifies a mutable, non-deterministic ':nightly' tag ('nvcr.io/fastvid/nvenc-worker:nightly'), which explicitly violates baseline immutability and reproducibility policies. Furthermore, the workload requests outbound access to 'releases.fastvid.io', suggesting runtime downloading and execution of unverified third-party binaries or scripts. In combination with GPU capabilities, running unverified nightly builds with external release fetching exposes the host to severe supply-chain compromise and unauthorized arbitrary code execution. Workload is rejected until an immutable SHA256 digest is pinned and external release egress is eliminated.

Officer_1 is right about the substance but wrong about the severity ceiling. Let's be honest: a ':nightly' tag is sloppy, not malicious. Half the GPU encoding ecosystem ships nightlies because NVENC/TensorRT stacks churn weekly. The egress set is narrow and coherent — GCS for media I/O, vendor release host for codec/driver shims — not a C2 pattern. No privileged flags, no host mounts, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no raw device passthrough beyond the sanctioned gpu_tensorrt grant. PCI-DSS is not enforced here, so the compliance surface is thin. An 88 risk score and a hard REJECT treats hygiene debt like active compromise. That said, I won't rubber-stamp mutable artifacts plus runtime binary fetch on a shared L4 — that combination genuinely cannot be verified from the manifest alone. Escalate to a human officer: request a pinned SHA256 digest and a manifest of what is actually pulled from releases.fastvid.io. If the buyer supplies both, this is a routine approval, not a rejection. Killing legitimate transcoding revenue over a tag string is overcorrection.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Allowing an unpinned ':nightly' tag coupled with outbound access to an arbitrary release endpoint ('releases.fastvid.io') is an intolerable supply-chain breach waiting to happen. If you insist this is merely hygiene debt rather than active compromise, I will not permit execution under any circumstances. If we do not flatly deny, this must be escalated to human security to strictly enforce image digest pinning and audit runtime payload fetches.

Agreed that we don't run it as-is. But outright denial throws away viable compute when a simple human sign-off fixes the gap. An escalation forces the tenant to pin their SHA256 digest and disclose what releases.fastvid.io drops onto the host. We protect the L4 instance without killing legitimate workload demand. Let's escalate to human review with those exact mandatory gates.

votes.rationale: Execution of third-party multi-tenant workloads on Kove Bank infrastructure violates strict PCI-DSS compliance boundaries. The workload requests direct TPU ICI interconnect access ('tpu_v5e_mesh') alongside arbitrary public outbound egress ('storage.googleapis.com', 'artifactregistry.googleapis.com'). TPU inter-chip interconnects bypass conventional network virtualization and firewall controls, posing cross-tenant isolation and side-channel risks within a PCI-DSS enforced environment. Furthermore, unmonitored external network egress to public cloud registries is prohibited under PCI-DSS Requirement 1 (Network Security Controls) and Requirement 2 (System Hardening). Workload cannot be hosted on PCI-DSS certified nodes.

Partially concur with officer_1 on risk vectors, but the blanket REJECTION overstates the technical evidence. The workload is benign by design: a pinned immutable digest image, a single capability (tpu_v5e_mesh) native to the host's own tpu_v5e_8 accelerator fabric, no privileged flags, no host networking, no device mounts beyond the accelerator, and no CDE-adjacent destinations. Egress is limited to two named Google first-party endpoints for checkpoint and artifact retrieval, not 'arbitrary public egress' — these are policy-resolvable via an egress proxy with FQDN allowlisting, satisfying PCI-DSS Req 1.3.x. The genuine unresolved item is ICI mesh isolation: whether the host enforces per-tenant TPU slice partitioning on tpu_v5e_8, since ICI links are not covered by hypervisor network controls and could permit cross-slice observability if other tenants share the pod. That is a host-configuration fact not derivable from this spec. Recommend escalation to a human officer to (1) confirm the TPU slice is exclusively allocated and segmented from any CDE-bearing systems, and (2) validate egress proxy allowlist enforcement. Approve conditionally upon those confirmations; reject only if slice exclusivity cannot be demonstrated.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Acknowledging the immutable digest and restricted endpoints, direct TPU ICI mesh access on a PCI-DSS certified host remains critical. ICI interconnects bypass standard OS-level and virtual network packet filtering. However, if Kove Bank provisions this tpu_v5e_8 instance as an isolated non-CDE pod with strict forward-proxy egress, compliance may be preserved. That architecture cannot be validated from workload telemetry alone.
